title: PsiTransfer
name: psitransfer
description: File sharing in the WeTransfer mould: drop in files, pick how long they last, and send the link. Big uploads resume after a dropped connection, downloads come as single files, zip or tar.gz, and links can be one-time or password protected. Source: https://github.com/psi-4ward/psitransfer

env.name: PSITRANSFER_UPLOAD_PASS
env.label: Upload password (required)
env.description: Anyone uploading needs this, so strangers can't fill your disk. Downloads don't. Anything long and hard to guess, or generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16

env.name: PSITRANSFER_ADMIN_PASS
env.label: Admin password (optional)
env.description: Turns on the /admin page, which lists every upload. Leave blank to keep it off, or generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16

env.name: PSITRANSFER_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the upload password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without one. Then open http://<your-host>:3030 (or whichever port you picked), enter it, drop in some files, pick a retention and hit Upload. The download link works for anyone who has it, no password needed unless you set one on that upload under Settings. Uploads last a week by default, and anything still there after 75 days is deleted whatever was picked. If you set an admin password, /admin lists every upload with its size and downloads. Files live as plain files in the psitransfer-data volume, so they survive updates. Changing either password on the form and redeploying swaps it. Docs: github.com/psi-4ward/psitransfer
